prerequisites: Integration in two and three dimensions

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the basis of general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Motion in a central force field.
teaching_methods: Theoretical approaches followed by applications in the form of exercises, problems, and laboratory practices
Detailed reading of the Study Guide and progressive advancement through the base text
Constant practice through self-assessment tests and Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: 0.8 * Final Exam Grade + 0.15 * Continuous Assessment Test Grade + 0.05 * Laboratory Practice Grade. To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 on the final exam is required if no Continuous Assessment Test is submitted. If a Continuous Assessment Test is submitted, a minimum of 3 on the final exam is required for its grade to be considered; if the Continuous Assessment Test is not submitted or its grade is lower than the final exam grade, only the final exam grade will be used. Laboratory practices are mandatory, and passing them is an essential condition to pass the course. An extraordinary exam is available in September for those who do not pass in June.
